name: ammonium hydrosulphide ice (no visible optical constants are published)
paper: L. A. Sromovsky, K. H. Baines, P. M. Fry and R. W. Carlson, "A possibly universal red chromophore for modeling color variations on Jupiter", Icarus 291 (2017) 232–244, DOI 10.1016/j.icarus.2016.12.014 (arXiv 1706.02779), §4.3 "Refractive index of main cloud layer", after the best-fit 1.85 of T. M. Sato, T. Satoh and Y. Kasaba 2013 (Icarus 222, 100–121, DOI 10.1016/j.icarus.2012.09.035), which Sromovsky et al. cite for Jovian clouds in the equatorial zone
source: a stated constant, not a measurement: Howett et al. 2007 (JOSA B 24, 126) measured NH4SH only over 1,300–12,000 cm⁻¹ (0.83–7.7 µm)
licence: a cited constant; no data set is used (decision-r08-licences.md row 5)
reduction: the constant on 380–780 nm every 5 nm
standIn: a non-absorbing particle of real index 1.80, constant over 380–780 nm: Sromovsky et al. 2017 write that an NH4SH-dominated main cloud's index would be closer to 1.8 and model it as conservative. A body whose medium shows this mode with less than CLOUD_DECK_SPLIT_OPTICAL_DEPTH above it at 550 nm reads ATMOSPHERE: APPROXIMATE, until measured visible constants replace it
